{{Quote|Gaharrag, Leurm, look who we have here.|Furan, upon the arrival of the new inmate Tahiri Veila|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
'''Gaharrag''' was an adult [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] who indulged in a life of crime prior to the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. His spree of [[Death/Legends|murder]] was brought to an end by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Tahiri Veila]], and Gaharrag earned a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] term at the [[Armand Isard Correctional Facility]]. In [[44 ABY]], he and several other inmates attempted to overwhelm the newly [[Trial of Tahiri Veila|incarcerated]] Veila, but all&mdash;Gaharrag included&mdash;were severely thrashed by the former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].

==Biography==
In the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], an adult [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] named Gaharrag enjoyed life as a criminal with a tendency toward [[Death/Legends|homicide]]. He donned markings reflective of the gang to which he belonged, and carved his own niche as a notorious killer&mdash;a reputation that was brought to an end through the efforts of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tahiri Veila]]. Following his arrest, trial, and subsequent conviction, the murderous Wookiee was remanded to [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Prison/Legends|penal]] service in the [[Armand Isard Correctional Facility]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. While incarcerated, Gaharrag made the acquaintance of many other criminals, among them a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] and fellow killer named [[Leurm]], and the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] vehicle thief [[Furan]].<ref name="Conviction" />

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> an opportunity for Gaharrag to avenge himself arose when Tahiri Veila, the same [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] responsible for his own incarceration, was herself [[Trial of Tahiri Veila|subjected]] to confinement within the walls of the Armand Isard Correctional Facility for her own crimes during the recent civil war. The Wookiee [[Gangster/Legends|gangster]] was enjoying a [[Time/Legends|time]] of recess when Veila was mistakenly brought to the same exercise yard occupied by the majority of the prison's male population&mdash;Gaharrag included. Furan was the first of them to confront her; when it became apparent that she would not be intimidated, Gaharrag, Leurm, and several other prisoners were summoned by the Mon Calamari to partake in her imminent demise.<ref name="Conviction" />

Taunting ensued as inmates prepared to attack, but Veila preceded them by assaulting Leurm and breaking his [[Limb/Legends|arm]]. The Wookiee charged and, as Veila faced him, swung, only to pummel Leurm as she ducked. With a great roar Gaharrag charged again as the Hutt fell and Veila eliminated a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] opponent. He attempted to seize the evasive [[Human/Legends|Human]] woman but was felled when she kicked and broke his right leg. Veila's victory was short-lived, however; while the battered tended to their injuries, prison staff dropped the former Jedi with a [[Stun/Legends|stun bolt]], one especially designed for the incapacitation of Wookiees like Gaharrag.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Personality and traits==
Gang [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoos]] occupied shaved patches of Gaharrag's coat, and he preferred to socialize with others who shared his proclivity for lawlessness. A well-known killer, Gaharrag earned a reputation with Jedi Tahiri Veila as one of the most dangerous criminals in whose conviction she was influential. His was an intimidating presence in combat, and he bellowed ceremonial Wookiee war cries designed to paralyze enemies with fear. Those with experience against Wookiee opponents recognized the fatality in failing to swiftly eliminate the threat Gaharrag posed and felt inclined to attack him first among a group of adversaries.<ref name="Conviction" />

While Veila's placement in the all-male exercise yard was expected by Gaharrag, who much desired to inflict bodily harm upon her, he was unprepared for the extent of her battle prowess and was repeatedly confounded by her evasive maneuvers. Despite his tremendous strength, considerable reach, and overall killing ability, Gaharrag was ultimately betrayed by his age, which was evidenced in the weak knee that Veila exploited to defeat him.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Behind the scenes==
Gaharrag appeared in ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'', a [[2011]] novel written by [[Aaron Allston]] as the seventh novel in the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series.<ref name="Conviction" />
